name: Banda, dialecte langwasi
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Tisserant, Charles. 1930. Essai sur la grammaire banda. (Travaux et mémoires de l'Institut d'ethnologie, XIII.) Paris: Institut d'ethnologie. 185 pp. Google Books H1cOAAAAYAAJ (Univ. of Virginia copy).
catalog_locator: Phonétique, section 'ACCENT', pp. 23-24 (p. 23 bottom third and p. 24 top four lines) of; cf. p. 19 on œ 'surtout dans des syllabes peu accentuées' and p. 5 for 'Dialecte langwasi'.
catalog_quote: La langue banda est chantée, c'est-à-dire, que chaque syllabe a sa tonalité propre, et est prononcée sur un ton plus élevé ou plus bas que la voisine. On distingue trois tons principaux: le ton haut, dans nó, dí, ká, tout, le ton moyen, dans enji, ils, le ton bas, dans mbwạ̀ngạ, palabre. Nous ne noterons ici la tonalité des éléments du langage que dans la mesure où la fonction du mot dans la phrase la fait varier: Le substantif verbal, joint au verbe, fait élever la tonalité de la voyelle de celui-ci: tee fú'fu, il est beau, en face de tee fu wa, id.; lobạn gé'gere, le pagne est grand, en face de lobạn gere wa. En dehors de l'accent de hauteur, il existe en banda un accent d'intensité qui affecte certaines syllabes des mots, en sorte que les syllabes non accentuées s'abrègent et ont une tendance à disparaître: Bĕleda, tronc d'arbre, bleda; temŏ, marque du futur, tem; marœ̆, faire, mar.

On distingue trois tons principaux : le ton haut, dans nó, dí, ká, tout, le ton moyen, dans enji, ils, le ton bas, dans mbwą̀ngą, palabre. new_statements.translation: The Banda language is 'sung', i.e. each syllable has its own pitch and is pronounced on a higher or lower tone than its neighbour. Three main tones are distinguished: high (nó, dí, ká 'all'), mid (enji 'they'), low (mbwąngą 'palaver'). [...] Apart from the pitch accent, there exists in Banda an intensity accent which affects certain syllables of words, so that the unaccented syllables shorten and tend to disappear: bĕleda 'tree trunk' > bleda; temŏ (future marker) > tem; marœ̆ 'to do' > mar.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Banda (all dialects treated together, Langwasi = Langbashe included) is a three-tone language; the author additionally reports a word-level intensity (stress) accent on 'certain syllables' whose complement syllables reduce or drop (examples show loss of an unstressed initial vowel in bĕleda > bleda and of unstressed final vowels in temŏ > tem, marœ̆ > mar), but he does not state which syllable carries it. Stress position therefore remains undescribed for Langbashe; the only positional rule in the older Banda literature (Cotel 1907: mostly penultimate, some final, a few antepenultimate) is explicitly for the Togbo dialect (togb1241).
new_statements.exceptions: None in Tisserant. (Cotel 1907, Togbo dialect only: lists of words with final accent -- kradzèy 'mollet', ubùn 'noir', sïmblïn 'crâne' etc. -- and a small set of trisyllables with antepenultimate accent -- bâmara 'lion', kúsara 'clou', tátara 'miroir'.)
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('certaines syllabes des mots'); citation forms; Tisserant marks tone only where grammatical function changes it and never marks the intensity accent in the body of the grammar. The statement is for 'la langue banda' as a whole in a multidialectal grammar whose 'banda' proper is the main dialect cluster (Linda/Togbo/Banda-Banda etc.), with Langwasi (Langbasi of the Ubangi banks between Kémo and Kouango, plus Langba and Mbugu/Ngbugu) treated as a distinct dialect cited throughout.
new_statements.identity_note: Tisserant 1930 is a pan-Banda grammar: its 'banda' is the main dialect cluster (Linda, Togbo, Banda-Banda, Gbaga, Yakpwa..), while 'dialecte langwasi' (p. 5: Länbwasi/längwasi on both banks of the Ubangi between Kémo and Kouango = Langbashe [lna] lang1318, plus Länba = Langba and Mbugu = Ngbugu, i.e. Glottolog's Ngbugu-Langbasi node sout2786) is treated as a distinct dialect cited 241 times; the accent statement (pp. 23-24) is made for the Banda language as a whole, not specifically for Langwasi. Cotel 1907's positional rule (mostly penultimate) is explicitly for the Togbo dialect of Sainte-Famille = Togbo-Vara Banda [tor] togb1241 and should be filed there, not under lang1318. The saved Tisserant page set also serves the other Banda world targets (togb1241, band1343, band1344, west2458..).
